301d9102a9a0a7a8.explanation: Bentley UXC's review (Kelli Mijares) says the team took notes as usual, used Otter to complement that process and filled gaps in their notes from the transcripts. It also says the transcripts were not accurate enough to share with the client sight unseen. One small caveat: the review also praises Otter's keyword search and synced audio, so the word 'only' is a slight simplification, but the gist is right.

evidence.quote: we conducted note-taking as we regularly would and relied on Otter to complement our existing process
we filled in any gaps in our notes by referring to timestamps of the text
While these were not accurate enough to share sight unseen with the client

687d3b71e1823874.claim: UMBC research office guidance warns that "Many, if not most, retain access to recorded information" and requires a signed confidentiality agreement from outside human transcriptionists kept in the protocol file.
687d3b71e1823874.quote: warns that "Many, if not most, retain access to recorded information,"
687d3b71e1823874.explanation: The UMBC page says word for word that external transcription services 'Many, if not most, retain access to recorded information.' It also says anyone other than the researcher who transcribes must sign a confidentiality agreement, and a copy must be kept in the investigator's protocol file.

evidence.quote: Many, if not most, retain access to recorded information.
a copy of this agreement must be kept in the investigator's protocol file.

7403b7cf5a1cf2d1.claim: University of Florida's ECE department allows Otter only on paid Business or Pro plans with a university email, does not approve the free plan, and excludes sensitive research data.
7403b7cf5a1cf2d1.quote: allows Otter only on paid Business or Pro plans with a university email, states the free plan is not approved, and excludes sensitive research data entirely
7403b7cf5a1cf2d1.explanation: The UF ECE guidelines require the Otter.ai Business or Pro plan and a @ufl.edu email address, and they say the Free Plan is not approved. They also bar recordings that include UF Sensitive Research or UF Restricted Data.

evidence.quote: Must utilize Otter.ai Business or Pro plan (Free Plan is not approved for use) and use @ufl.edu email address
Content recorded must NOT include UF Sensitive Research or UF Restricted Data

fbc5f27baeec42d8.claim: NVivo Transcription is a cloud service that uploads audio to the vendor's online platform.
fbc5f27baeec42d8.quote: NVivo Transcription is itself a cloud service: audio is uploaded to the vendor's online platform
fbc5f27baeec42d8.explanation: Lumivero/QSR describes NVivo Transcription as an automated cloud service where media is transcribed through an online portal. York also says audio files are uploaded to the online platform and data is stored in the cloud.

evidence.quote: NVivo Transcription is an automated service to transcribe media files from within NVivo, or directly through an online portal.
Audio files uploaded to the online platform are transcribed in a time-span of half the length of the audio.

51557da8eef8d565.claim: The University of York allows NVivo Transcription only in limited cases with anonymised data after a data protection impact assessment.
51557da8eef8d565.quote: allows it only in limited cases with anonymised data, after a data protection impact assessment
51557da8eef8d565.explanation: York's IT Services page says NVivo Transcription doesn't meet its security standards and can only be used in a limited number of cases where the data is anonymised. Users need to complete a DPIA first, though the page also allows that a DPIA may be agreed not to be required.

evidence.quote: It can only be used in a limited number of cases, where data is anonymised.
Once a DPIA is signed off (or agreed to not be a requirement) then you can purchase licences

717d33c8feeed078.claim: NVivo, ATLAS.ti and MAXQDA all import Word documents and plain text files.
717d33c8feeed078.quote: NVivo, ATLAS.ti and MAXQDA all import Word documents and plain text
717d33c8feeed078.explanation: The official documentation for all three tools lists Word (DOC/DOCX) and plain text (TXT) as text formats they can import.

evidence.quote: Importable Text formats: RTF/D, DOC/X, ODT, PDF, TXT, HTML
MS Word | .doc; .docx; .rtf ... Plain text | .txt
Microsoft Word Document (docx) ... Rich text (rtf) Plain text (txt)
